sourceObjectiveEnglish: Count, tell time, and give measurements and quantities on the job

sourceSpeakingEnglish: Tell the crew lead what time you start, how many bundles you need, and one measurement.

cards.reviewNote: The source means a US pound in this job measurement. French livre can mean an imperial pound in Quebec and a colloquial 500 g in France; choose locale and exact unit notation before scoring or recording.
The source means a bundle of shingles. Archived paquet is a general package; select the job/supplier headword and quantity context with qualified roofing terminology review.

reader.sourceSpanish: Empezamos a las seis de la mañana.

reader.sourceSpanish: El camión llega en veinte minutos.
reader.sourceEnglish: The truck arrives in twenty minutes.
reader.conditionalFrench: Le camion arrive dans vingt minutes.

reader.sourceEnglish: How many bundles do we need today?

reader.sourceEnglish: We need thirty bundles of shingles.
reader.archivedFrench: On a besoin de trente paquets de bardeaux.
reader.reviewNote: Thirty bundles of shingles uses the same unresolved trade headword as card 6; keep the source quantity and material exact.

reader.sourceSpanish: Cada bulto pesa unas setenta libras.
reader.sourceEnglish: Each bundle weighs about seventy pounds.
reader.archivedFrench: Chaque paquet pèse environ soixante-dix livres.
reader.reviewNote: Seventy US pounds must not become an unqualified French 500 g livre; decide locale and unit expression before selecting a French line.

reader.archivedFrench: Le mur mesure dix pieds, ou à peu près trois mètres.

reader.conditionalFrench: Le clou fait un pouce et demi de long.

archivedRegionalNotesEnglish: US crews may use feet, inches and pounds; French sites generally use metric, while Quebec construction often uses imperial measures. Confirm job documents and spoken units.
Belgian and Swiss number words may use septante/nonante; this lesson uses soixante-dix/quatre-vingt-dix.
The reading’s bundle weight is an example, not a product specification.

speakingEvidence.archivedFrenchOpening: On commence à sept heures. J’ai besoin de vingt paquets de bardeaux. Le clou fait un pouce et demi de long.
